title: Wavepacket photodetection and normally ordered correlations

items.title: One-mode photon number operator and count PVM

references.title: Daniel A. Steck, Quantum and Atom Optics, revision 0.16.10 (27 June 2026), Chapter 16
references.locator: Author-hosted complete course text, §16.4.2.2, PDF pp. 691–692, for normalized pulse-mode creation operators. The count PVM and operator domains below are constructed locally.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear pairing used for bosonic Fock space, and let $u\in H$ satisfy $\|u\|=1$. Put $K=u^\perp$. Let $J_u:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C u)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(K)\to\mathcal F_s(H)$ be the one-mode Fock unitary, and for $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let $e_n=u^{\otimes n}\in(\mathbb C u)_s^{(n)}$, with $e_0=1$. On $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C u)$ define $Q_n z=\langle e_n,z\rangle_2e_n$, and on $\mathcal F_s(H)$ put
$$P_n:=J_u(Q_n\otimes I)J_u^{-1}.$$
For every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, define the strong sum
$$E_u(B):=\sum_{n\in B\cap\mathbb N_0}P_n.$$
Define the mode number operator
$$N_u:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}nP_n,\qquad D(N_u):=\left\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^2\|P_n\Psi\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
Then $(P_n)_{n\ge0}$ are mutually orthogonal projections with strong sum $I$, $E_u$ is a projection-valued measure supported on $\mathbb N_0$, and $N_u$ is self-adjoint with these spectral projections. Define $M_u\Psi:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n(n-1)P_n\Psi$ on
$$D(M_u):=\left\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n^2(n-1)^2\|P_n\Psi\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
Then $M_u=N_u(N_u-I)$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a graph core for it. On the finite-particle subspace,
$$N_u=a^\dagger(u)a(u),\qquad M_u=N_u(N_u-I)=a^\dagger(u)^2a(u)^2.$$
Thus the finite-particle restriction of $a^\dagger(u)^2a(u)^2$ is essentially self-adjoint with closure $M_u$.

items.title: Ideal wavepacket number counting

references.title: Roy J. Glauber, The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence, Physical Review 130, 2529–2539 (1963)
references.locator: §II, printed pp. 2530–2532, equations (2.14)–(2.18), and §III, pp. 2532–2534, equations (3.1)–(3.7), for ideal absorption and normally ordered count correlations. The local postulate uses a countable mode PVM, not point-field products.

references.title: Daniel A. Steck, Quantum and Atom Optics, revision 0.16.10 (27 June 2026)
references.locator: Author-hosted complete course text, Chapter 16 §§16.1 and 16.4.2.2–16.4.2.3, PDF pp. 685–693, for photodetection, normalized pulse modes and time-window counting. Its narrowband and finite-window assumptions are not imported as exact claims here.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the positive transverse free-photon model whose one-particle space is $\mathcal H_T=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$ with its transverse condition and whose state space is the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$. In the unit convention where $\mathbf k$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$, let $u\in\mathcal H_T^\nu$ be a normalized transverse wavepacket for the invariant measure $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2|\mathbf k|)$, so that $u(\mathbf k)$ has unit metre and $\int|u|^2d\nu=1$. Let $v=Wu$, where $Wf(\mathbf k)=f(\mathbf k)/\sqrt{2|\mathbf k|}$; then $v\in\mathcal H_T$, $v(\mathbf k)$ has unit $\mathrm m^{3/2}$, and $\|v\|_2=1$. In the Fock factorization $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)\cong\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C v)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(v^\perp)$, $P_n(v)$ is the orthogonal projection onto mode occupation $n$ tensored with the identity on the orthogonal-mode Fock factor. These projections are mutually orthogonal and have strong sum $I$; their count PVM is $E_v(B)=\sum_{n\in B\cap\mathbb N_0}P_n(v)$, and $N_v=\sum_n nP_n(v)$ on the domain $\sum_n n^2\|P_n(v)\Psi\|^2<\infty$. A density operator $\rho$ means a positive self-adjoint trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, using the trace pairing obtained from the Fock space's second-variable-linear convention by conjugation. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$, put $p_n=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_n(v))$. The mathematical density/PVM result makes $(p_n)$ a countably additive probability law under the stated Countable Choice hypothesis.

Adopt as the ideal detector postulate that this law is the model probability for recording exactly $n$ photons in the selected mode. The detector is number resolving, has unit mode efficiency, and has no mode mismatch, background counts or dark counts. This is an additional physical measurement assumption; it is not deduced from the CCR or from the free-field equations.

When $\sum_n np_n<\infty$ and $\sum_n n(n-1)p_n<\infty$, define the first number moment and normally ordered second factorial moment by
$$\mu_v(\rho):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}np_n,\qquad F^{(2)}_v(\rho):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n(n-1)p_n.$$
The PVM sums define the unbounded-state moments. In this ideal mode model, define the normally ordered second-mode correlation to be the spectral factorial expectation $F^{(2)}_v(\rho)$. The self-adjoint closure of the finite-particle operator $a^\dagger(v)^2a(v)^2$ is $N_v(N_v-I)$ by [[lem-qftx-mode-number-pvm]], so this definition agrees with the normally ordered operator on its finite-particle core and uses the spectral expectation for states outside that core. It does not assert a trace product of $\rho$ with an unbounded operator. If $\mu_v(\rho)>0$, define the dimensionless same-mode zero-delay statistic
$$g_v^{(2)}(0):=\frac{F^{(2)}_v(\rho)}{\mu_v(\rho)^2}.$$
Here $0$ is the conventional zero-delay label for this same-mode statistic; no temporal detector response or pointwise product of electric-field distributions is defined.
items.physical_scope: An ideal countably number-resolving detector for one normalized transverse wavepacket mode in the selected positive free-photon Fock model, with unit efficiency, no mode mismatch, no background and no dark counts. It supplies no finite-time response, point-field product, interacting QED model, or empirical outcome.

items.title: Ideal one-mode intensity correlations separate model states

references.title: Roy J. Glauber, The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence, Physical Review 130, 2529–2539 (1963)
references.locator: §II equations (2.15)–(2.18), §III equations (3.6)–(3.14), and §IV equations (4.8)–(4.10), printed pp. 2531–2536, for normal-ordered photodetection correlations and coherent-field context. Number-state and geometric-law calculations are proved locally.

references.title: Daniel A. Steck, Quantum and Atom Optics, revision 0.16.10 (27 June 2026)
references.locator: Author-hosted complete course text, Chapter 2 §§2.6.1–2.6.2, PDF pp. 74–76, for second-order coherence, the explicit Gaussian thermal-field assumption and its g^(2)(0)=2 consequence; Chapter 16 §16.1, PDF pp. 685–686, for normal ordering. The local theorem separately proves the quantum geometric-mode calculation.

items.statement:
Assume the ideal wavepacket counting postulate for a normalized mode $v$, and let $p_n$ be the resulting count law of a prepared state. Write
$$\mu:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}np_n,\qquad F_2:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n(n-1)p_n,\qquad g_v^{(2)}(0):=F_2/\mu^2$$
when $0<\mu<\infty$ and $F_2<\infty$. Let $J_v:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C v)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(v^\perp)\to\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$ be the one-mode Fock unitary, let $|n\rangle_v=v^{\otimes n}$ with $|0\rangle_v=1$, and let $\Omega_{v^\perp}$ be the vacuum in $\mathcal F_s(v^\perp)$. Put $\psi_n:=J_v(|n\rangle_v\otimes\Omega_{v^\perp})$. For a unit vector $\psi$, $g_v^{(2)}(0;\psi)$ denotes the postulate's value for the pure density operator $|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ put $\lambda=|\alpha|^2$, $Z_\lambda=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\lambda^n/n!$, and define the coherent-mode vector
$$\psi_\alpha:=Z_\lambda^{-1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\alpha^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\psi_n.$$
For $m\ge1$, the number preparation is $\psi_m$. For $0<r<1$, the geometric one-mode state is
$$\rho_r:=(1-r)\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}r^n|\psi_n\rangle\langle\psi_n|.$$
Then the ideal model predictions are
$$g_v^{(2)}(0;\psi_\alpha)=1,\qquad g_v^{(2)}(0;\psi_m)=1-\frac1m,\qquad g_v^{(2)}(0;\rho_r)=2.$$
The final state has the specified single-mode geometric occupation law; these conclusions do not classify all radiation as coherent, number, or thermal.
items.physical_scope: Exact model predictions for coherent-mode, fixed-number and geometric one-mode preparations under ideal wavepacket number counting. The geometric distribution is the specified single-mode thermal occupation law; no universal classification of radiation or empirical outcome is asserted.

items.title: Ideal independent loss preserves normalized factorial correlation

references.title: Daniel A. Steck, Quantum and Atom Optics, revision 0.16.10 (27 June 2026)
references.locator: Author-hosted complete course text, Chapter 16 §§16.2–16.4.1, PDF pp. 687–690, for lossless beam-splitter mode transformations and the binomial output law for photons in one input. The theorem explicitly assumes independent fixed-efficiency thinning and proves its moment identities locally.

references.title: Roy J. Glauber, The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence, Physical Review 130, 2529–2539 (1963)
references.locator: §II equations (2.16)–(2.18), printed pp. 2531–2532, for coincidence-count correlation functions. No loss or efficiency law is imported from this paper.

items.statement:
Assume the ideal wavepacket-counting postulate for a selected mode $v\in\mathcal H_T$ with $\|v\|=1$, and let $\rho$ be the incoming density operator on $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$ (a positive self-adjoint trace-class operator with trace one). By that postulate, $P_n(v)$ are the mode-count projections and $p_n=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_n(v))$ are the count probabilities, so $p_n\ge0$ and $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_n=1$. Define the incoming mean and second factorial moment by
$$\mu:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}np_n,\qquad F_2:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}n(n-1)p_n,$$
and assume $0<\mu<\infty$ and $F_2<\infty$. Define $g_N^{(2)}(0):=F_2/\mu^2$; for this input state $\rho$, the postulate denotes the same statistic by $g_v^{(2)}(0)$.

Let $0<\eta\le1$ be a dimensionless fixed efficiency and assume no background or dark counts. To specify independent recording, put $b_\eta(0)=1-\eta$, $b_\eta(1)=\eta$, and
$$\Omega:=\{(n,x):n\in\mathbb N_0,\ x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{0,1\}^n\},\qquad \mathcal A:=\mathcal P(\Omega).$$
This is countable under the explicit encoding $(n,x)\mapsto(n,\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j2^{j-1})$. Give the space the point masses
$$\mathbb P(\{(n,x)\}):=p_n\prod_{j=1}^{n}b_\eta(x_j),$$
where the empty product for $n=0$ is $1$. For each fixed $n$, the product factors define the conditional product law $Q_n$ on $\{0,1\}^n$; hence its coordinates are independent Bernoulli variables with success probability $\eta$. Since $\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}Q_n(\{x\})=(\eta+(1-\eta))^n=1$, these point masses sum to one and define a probability measure $\mathbb P$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal A)$. Define $N(n,x):=n$ and $K(n,x):=\sum_{j=1}^n x_j$. For every nonnegative random variable $Y$ on this space, use the expectation
$$\mathbb E Y:=\sum_{(n,x)\in\Omega}Y(n,x)\,\mathbb P(\{(n,x)\}).$$
The marginal law of $N$ is $(p_n)$, and the conditional count law of $K$ given $N=n$ is the binomial law induced by $Q_n$. If $\mathbb E K>0$, define $g_K^{(2)}(0):=\mathbb E[K(K-1)]/(\mathbb E K)^2$. Then
$$\mathbb E K=\eta\mu,\qquad \mathbb E[K(K-1)]=\eta^2F_2.$$
Consequently the normalized zero-delay factorial correlation is unchanged:
$$g_K^{(2)}(0)=\frac{\mathbb E[K(K-1)]}{(\mathbb E K)^2}=\frac{F_2}{\mu^2}=g_N^{(2)}(0)=g_v^{(2)}(0).$$
This is a model deduction conditional on independent constant-efficiency thinning; it is not a universal property of real detectors.
items.physical_scope: A selected mode with a finite positive ideal mean is sent through an explicitly assumed independent, constant-efficiency counting channel with no background or dark counts. The theorem does not model detector dead time, mode dependence, correlated loss, or actual measured data.

title: Wavepacket photodetection and normally ordered correlations — Examples

items.title: One-photon wavepacket has zero ideal same-mode factorial correlation

references.title: Daniel A. Steck, Quantum and Atom Optics, revision 0.16.10 (27 June 2026)
references.locator: Author-hosted complete course text, Chapter 16 §16.3, PDF pp. 687–688, one-photon beam-splitter output and zero ideal joint-detection probability; the same section identifies accidental coincidences, finite detection times and dark counts as real limitations.

references.title: Roy J. Glauber, The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence, Physical Review 130, 2529–2539 (1963)
references.locator: §II equations (2.16)–(2.18), printed pp. 2531–2532, for the normal-ordered two-count correlation that vanishes when fewer than two photons are available.

items.statement: Assume the ideal mode-counting and thinning models. Prepare the normalized one-photon state $\psi_1$ in the selected transverse mode, with all orthogonal modes in vacuum, and take $0<\eta\le1$. The ideal count law has $N=1$, so its mean is $1$ and its same-mode zero-delay factorial correlation is $g_N^{(2)}(0)=0$. After independent loss, the registered count is Bernoulli with $\mathbb P(K=1)=\eta$ and $\mathbb P(K=0)=1-\eta$, with mean $\eta$ and $g_K^{(2)}(0)=0$. This example is conditional on the one-mode and no-background assumptions and does not assert zero coincidence probability for arbitrary multimode detectors.
items.physical_scope: One exactly prepared photon in one normalized transverse mode, counted by the ideal number-resolving model with optional independent fixed-efficiency loss. It asserts no zero coincidence probability for arbitrary multimode detectors or apparatus with background.
